## Upgrading to 1.0.0

- **Existing pre-release users** (`1.0.0-alpha.x`, `1.0.0-beta.1` to `1.0.0-beta.3`, npm or native): nothing to do. Specforce updates itself to 1.0.0 in the background after an interactive command. To get it right away on an npm install, in your terminal:

  ```bash
  npm install -g @jeancodogno/specforce-kit@latest
  ```

- **Coming from 0.2.x** (which has no auto-update): follow [Migrating from 0.2.x](https://github.com/jeancodogno/specforce-kit/blob/v1.0.0/CHANGELOG.md#migrating-from-02x) in the changelog (re-run `specforce init`, then invoke skills by name instead of the old slash commands).

## Highlights

- Native skills (`spf.discovery`, `spf.spec`, `spf.constitution`, `spf.implement`, `spf.archive`) replace the old slash commands and subagents.
- Tiered spec sizes, module deltas that keep the module living specs current, and an independent QA verdict before archiving.
- Background auto-update with checksum verification for native binaries, plus, from 1.0.0 onward, a one-time notice when a stable release is available to npm pre-release users.
- Cursor support; Gemini CLI support and the project memorial are removed.
- Every npm package is published with provenance.

The full list of changes is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/jeancodogno/specforce-kit/blob/v1.0.0/CHANGELOG.md).
